title: Galilean and special relativity
summary: Reference frames, Galilean transformations, Einstein’s postulates, Lorentz transformations, time dilation, length contraction, relativity of simultaneity and spacetime diagrams.

keyterms.definition: A frame moving at constant velocity, in which Newton’s first law holds.
Classical conversion between frames: x′ = x − vt, t′ = t, u′ = u − v.
The laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames; the speed of light in vacuum is the same for all inertial observers.
γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²); always ≥ 1, becoming large as v approaches c.
Time interval between two events measured in the frame where they occur at the same place; the shortest measured interval.
A moving clock runs slow: Δt = γΔt₀, where Δt₀ is the proper time.
Length of an object measured in its own rest frame; the longest measured length.
A moving object is shorter along its motion: L = L₀/γ.
Events simultaneous in one frame are generally not simultaneous in another if they occur at different places.
(Δs)² = (cΔt)² − (Δx)²; the same in every inertial frame.
The path of an object on a spacetime diagram; light worldlines are at 45° when ct and x use equal scales.

lessons.title: Frames, postulates and the Lorentz factor

questions.prompt: A train moves at 30 m s⁻¹. A passenger walks forward at 2 m s⁻¹ relative to the train. Using Galilean relativity, her speed relative to the ground is
questions.explanation: Galilean velocity addition: u = u′ + v = 2 + 30 = 32 m s⁻¹.

questions.statement: According to Galilean relativity, light from a moving lamp would travel at c + v relative to the ground.
questions.explanation: Galilean addition predicts c + v; experiments show light always travels at c, which is why special relativity was needed.

questions.text: In special relativity the speed of light in a vacuum is the ___ for all inertial observers.
questions.explanation: This is Einstein’s second postulate, consistent with Maxwell’s equations and experiment.

questions.prompt: What is the Lorentz factor for a speed of 0.60c?
What is the Lorentz factor for a speed of 0.80c?

questions.statement: Newton’s first law is valid in an accelerating reference frame.
questions.explanation: Newton’s laws hold only in inertial frames; accelerating frames need fictitious forces.

questions.prompt: Match each equation to its name.
questions.explanation: The Lorentz transformations reduce to the Galilean ones when v ≪ c (γ ≈ 1).

questions.text: Two spaceships approach each other, each at 0.50c relative to Earth. Relativistic addition gives their relative speed as ___ c.

questions.prompt: Which experiment’s null result supported the idea that light speed does not depend on the observer’s motion?
questions.explanation: Michelson–Morley found no change in light speed due to Earth’s motion through a supposed ether.

questions.prompt: As v → c, the Lorentz factor
questions.explanation: 1 − v²/c² → 0, so γ → ∞: no massive object can be accelerated to c.

lessons.title: Time dilation, length contraction and spacetime

questions.prompt: A muon lives 2.2 µs in its rest frame and moves at 0.995c (γ = 10). Its lifetime measured from Earth is
questions.explanation: Δt = γΔt₀ = 10 × 2.2 µs = 22 µs, allowing muons from the upper atmosphere to reach the ground.

questions.text: A spaceship has proper length 100 m. When it passes Earth at 0.60c (γ = 1.25), Earth observers measure its length as ___ m.

questions.statement: Proper time is measured by a clock that is present at both events.
questions.explanation: If both events occur at the same place in a frame, a single clock there records the proper time.

questions.prompt: In the muon’s own frame, why does it reach the ground before decaying?
questions.explanation: In the muon frame it lives only 2.2 µs, but the atmosphere rushing past is contracted by γ, so the distance is short.

questions.statement: Two events that are simultaneous in one inertial frame are simultaneous in all inertial frames.
questions.explanation: Simultaneity is relative for events at different locations.

questions.prompt: On a spacetime diagram with ct vertical and x horizontal (equal scales), the worldline of a light pulse is at
options: an angle depending on the observer
questions.explanation: Light covers Δx = cΔt, so its worldline has gradient 1, i.e. 45°, in every frame.

questions.text: The quantity (cΔt)² − (Δx)², which all inertial observers agree on, is called the spacetime ___.
questions.explanation: The spacetime interval is invariant even though Δt and Δx individually differ between frames.

questions.prompt: For a moving frame S′ drawn on the spacetime diagram of S, the ct′ axis is
options: tilted towards the light line by angle θ with tan θ = v/c
questions.explanation: The ct′ axis is the worldline of the S′ origin, tilted from ct by θ where tan θ = v/c; the x′ axis tilts by the same angle from x.

questions.prompt: Match each effect to its equation.
questions.explanation: All these follow from the Lorentz transformations.

questions.prompt: Order the steps in a time-dilation problem.
items: Find the frame where they occur at the same place
Call that time the proper time Δt₀
Calculate Δt = γΔt₀ for the other frame
questions.explanation: Identifying the proper time first avoids applying γ the wrong way round.
